SECURITY, and it is the gate he set. VERIFIED 2026-07-29, every step checked by hand. His GitHub sync token is stored in plain text in localStorage (src/task-board.js:679). localStorage is scoped to an ORIGIN, not a folder, so the hosted app at https://evrenucar.github.io/punchlist_app/ shares one localStorage with every other Pages site on the account: clocktest, kora_aerospace_web, nokta_labs_website_v1, proto_website, thermal-cam, website. Any script on any of them can read the token, which has read and write on his private board repo. AND ONE OF THEM ALREADY LOADS UNPINNED THIRD-PARTY CODE: nokta_labs_website_v1 has <script src="https://unpkg.com/lucide@latest">, so whatever that package publishes next executes on his origin forever. This does not need him to be targeted, it needs the supply chain to have one bad day. HIS ANSWERS 2026-07-29: "lets make it secure, I don't have a custom domain for now but it would be nice to to do that lets have it as priority item" and "make sure the private keys can't be read by anyone". So: own origin is the direction, custom domain is a PRIORITY item but not available today, and a free own-origin route has to carry it until then. He also asked, fairly, what an unrelated site has to do with any of this. PROVEN ON HIS OWN SITES, in a scratch profile: standing on nokta_labs_website_v1 I wrote into Punchlist's sync slot, then opened Punchlist and read it back. Same origin, one storage. It is not only readable, it is WRITABLE, so a hostile script could repoint his sync at its own repo and his next push would hand over the board.

children.text: PRIORITY, his word: a custom domain for Punchlist. Own origin, own localStorage, and the six siblings can never see the token or the signing key. He does not have a domain yet, so this is the direction rather than today's step.

Until the domain exists, the free route to the same result: host the hosted copy on an origin of its own. A GitHub ORGANISATION gives punchlist.github.io style hosting for nothing and stays on GitHub, or a free Pages host does the same. Either way it is a different hostname, which is all the browser cares about.

HIS INSTRUCTION: "make sure the private keys can't be read by anyone". Note this is BOTH secrets, not one: the sync token and the board's identity signing key both live in the same shared localStorage. Own origin fixes both at once. Nothing short of it does, because any script on the origin can read any key.

Ten-minute mitigation still worth doing whatever else happens: pin or remove the unpkg lucide@latest script on nokta_labs_website_v1. It closes the one hole that exists today. It does not close the class, because any future script on any of the seven sites reopens it.
Mitigation available today, ten minutes: pin or remove the unpkg lucide@latest script on nokta_labs_website_v1. Closes the known hole, does not fix the class.
Real fix: Punchlist on its own origin. Separate origin means separate localStorage, and the other six can never see the token. Needs his call on custom domain versus separate account.
Note for whoever writes the guide afterwards: a downloaded copy is already safe here, because file:// is its own origin. Only the hosted copy has this problem.

THE GATE ONLY WORKS BECAUSE OF .gitattributes: the build stamps the real byte count into the landing page, Windows CRLF measured 436,274 bytes while Pages serves the LF file at 433,199, so the gate failed on 12 of the last 12 commits including docs-only ones. LF is pinned now, the worktree renormalized, and the landing page finally advertises the size people actually download (423 KB, not 426). Gate verified both ways: green on a clean tree, exit 1 on a src change with no rebuild.

DONE 2026-07-29 (v1.5.41). P1 MONOLITH. 8,151 lines cut into 25 numbered parts under src/app that the build concatenates in order. A CUT, not a rewrite: no line moved, the migration refused to write until the parts concatenated back byte-identical, and the built file then differed by one line, the version stamp. No module system, no bundler, one script scope, exactly as before.

NEXT PASS, not urgent: a few parts are mixed rather than pure. 16-rendering-parts carries migrateState and normalizeState because they sit in the middle of the render helpers. Sorting functions into their proper part means REORDERING, which is the risky half, so it goes one move at a time with the suite green. The safe half is already banked.

CAUGHT BY THE SPLIT, fixed the same hour: the build's version anchor could not tell a file move from a milestone bump (git log -G matches an added line either way), so the patch count reset and it stamped v1.5.0 onto a v1.5.40 app. --diff-filter=M fixes it: a bump modifies the constant, a move only adds it. Same wrong number the Pages workflow already warns about from a shallow clone.

P1 UPDATE CHANNEL: update detection is coupled to GitHub Releases, and that is exactly how 24 builds shipped with nobody told (releases/latest sat at v1.5.1 from Jul 19). Fix: the build writes website/latest.json {version, download, notes}, and a downloaded copy checks THAT instead of releases/latest. Two separate ideas afterwards: latest.json is the latest deployed build, a Release is a stable milestone you cut when you mean it.

KEEP (the audit's own conclusion, worth quoting back at anyone who proposes a rewrite): "Do not rebuild the application architecture from scratch." Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no required server, one distributable HTML file, localStorage as the default, GitHub sync optional, the simple Node build script. A framework, a backend, or a conventional multi-file web app would make Punchlist worse, not better.

WHAT IT IS, in one line, so this item alone is enough to remember why it mattered: reminders were never the feature. His sentence was "I never forget. I just do not start." What he actually described is a DAY STRIP (now, next, slipped) and RECURRENCE (daily habits, which he called the real missing piece). children.text: THE FEATURE, his words: "A day strip. What is now, what is next, what slipped." Three answers to three questions he actually asks, one line at the top of the board. NOW answers "I lose the block, the work was meant for 2pm". NEXT answers "I remember late, at 11pm, when I can no longer do it". SLIPPED is the quiet line instead of the popup he did not want. It is a view over tasks that already have a time: it stores nothing new.

RECURRENCE, and he called it himself: "Yes, daily habits. That is the real missing piece." Plus weekly standing meetings. The trap is that a repeating task cannot be one row you tick, because ticking it destroys the thing that must come back. Model is a RULE that produces INSTANCES: only today's instance is on the board, ticking never touches the rule.

WHAT FIRES: "Punchlist only, while open. I accept that it misses things." So one quiet in-tab line, no popups, no sound. On opening after a gap: "One quiet line. Three were due while you were away. No popups." Real notifications are a separate later decision and need an app per platform to be honest, which he noted as "maybe direct notifications could be done later".

OPEN, and he asked for a diagram before answering: should a reminder be a THIRD time alongside date and start time? Diagram is at /daystrip. Given that what stops him today is "Too many steps to reach the field", the cheap options are no third time at all, or an offset like "10 minutes before", which is one dropdown.
BLOCKED BY, his words: "Nothing today, but I want it back after the day shape work lands." Nothing here works until setting and seeing a task's time is easy. Day shape comes first.
ON HOLD with the rest of this: when and if the strip ever lands, delete the current reminder implementation. Nothing to do while this is shelved, and the current one stays exactly where it is.
